headline: QA Morning Signal — 2026-09-18: model-misalignment reporting, Android Bench 2.0, device-state libs, and GitHub Actions updates

top_signal.title: OpenAI publishes a model misalignment reporting framework plus six incident reports
top_signal.summary: OpenAI released a formal framework for tracking, investigating, and publicly reporting model misalignment, and published six recent incident reports that document unexpected or concerning model behaviour and investigation workflows.
top_signal.why_it_matters: QA teams testing LLM-powered features get a concrete disclosure and incident taxonomy to design failure detection, triage playbooks, and acceptance criteria for model regressions and safety bugs.

items.title: Android Bench 2.0 adds long‑horizon tasks, multimodal verification, and agent harness comparisons
items.summary: Android Bench 2.0 introduces challenging long‑horizon tasks, a multimodal visual judge, multi‑harness evaluations, and continuous completion metrics to measure how LLMs and agents help with real Android engineering work.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a reproducible benchmark and harness practices QA teams can adopt for evaluating agentic developer tools, visual UI checks, and LLM-driven change impact on app codebases.

items.title: AndroidX Security State libraries provide a unified device security and update view
items.summary: AndroidX Security State (stable) and Security State Provider (1.0.0) expose standardized APIs to report device security posture and pending OS/patch availability across OEMs and providers.
items.why_it_matters: Mobile test orchestration and device-farm selection can now gate tests or triage failures by device update/security state, reducing noisy failures from unpatched or insecure device conditions.

items.title: Ubuntu 26 runner image for GitHub Actions is generally available (x64 and arm64)
items.summary: GitHub Actions now supports Ubuntu 26.04 runner images in GA for both x64 and arm64, graduating from public preview and replacing older Ubuntu runner images on the hosted fleet.
items.why_it_matters: Test matrices, toolchains, and dependency packaging can behave differently on Ubuntu 26 or arm64; QA leads should validate CI images, pin critical tool versions, and update reproducibility tests.

items.title: Workflow execution protections for GitHub Actions reach general availability
items.summary: GitHub made workflow execution protections generally available: actor/event allowlists, workflow-file targeting, Insights, and a REST API — plus a default evaluate-mode rule to disable pull_request_target for public repos.
items.why_it_matters: Policy enforcement can silently block or change who can run tests; QA should run evaluate mode, audit impacted workflows, and update gating and allowlists to avoid unexpected CI failures.

watch.title: Agentic CLI customizations added to Copilot usage metrics API
watch.summary: GitHub Copilot’s usage metrics API now reports agentic activity (skills, custom agents, MCP servers, slash commands, plugins) in per-user and aggregate reports to help admins measure adoption.
watch.why_it_matters: If your org uses agentic tools for test generation or execution, these metrics let QA and engineering managers monitor adoption, spot risky agent usage, and tie automation quality to business metrics.

learning.title: JetBrains: Building a RAG pipeline for semantic code search (developer diary, part 1)
learning.category: AI for QA / RAG evaluation techniques
learning.summary: JetBrains published a developer‑diary on productionizing a RAG pipeline for semantic code search, covering parsing, chunking, and vectorization decisions that affect retrieval quality for coding agents.
learning.why_it_matters: QA and automation engineers building agentic test assistants or evidence-backed validators should learn these RAG tradeoffs to improve recall, citation reliability, and reduce hallucinated test fixes.
